 Eddie Vedder, Hozier and Celebrity Supporters Help Raise Over $3 Million for EB Research
 November 20, 2026 
 From left to right: Michael Hund, CEO of EB Research Partnership; Olivia Vedder; Hozier; Eddie Vedder and Jill Vedder, co-founders of EB Research Partnership; and Colin Farrell at Venture Into Cures. Photo credit: Sachyn Mital
 EB Research Partnership (EBRP), a nonprofit organization dedicated to finding a cure for epidermolysis bullosa (EB), raised more than $3 million during its annual Venture Into Cures gala in New York City, bringing together nearly 700 supporters, researchers, healthcare leaders and entertainment figures.
 Held November 11, 2026, at Pier Sixty, the fundraising event featured appearances by Eddie Vedder, Hozier, Colin Farrell and Tom Holland, alongside families affected by the rare genetic disease.
 Epidermolysis bullosa, commonly known as Butterfly Disease, causes extreme skin fragility, resulting in painful blistering and tearing from minor contact. Although there is currently no cure, advances in medical research have led to new treatments and expanded clinical trials.
 EBRP co-founders Jill and Eddie Vedder joined patients, families and scientists to recognize recent progress and generate additional funding for research.
 “We have reached a remarkable moment in EB, progress that once seemed impossible is now happening before our eyes,” said Michael Hund , CEO of EB Research Partnership.
 “We have gone from zero FDA-approved treatments to three, while clinical trials have increased 25-fold.”
 The evening included a surprise three-song performance by Irish singer-songwriter Hozier, introduced by Eddie Vedder.
 Comedian Sam Morril opened the program, while television personality Liz Trinnear, who lives with EB simplex, served as host.
 Actor Tom Holland, who previously hosted the gala in 2021, delivered a video message introducing a film highlighting the organization’s impact.
 Academy Award-nominated actor Colin Farrell also attended in support of the EB community. His documentary The Slightest Touch , exploring his friendship with EB advocate Emma Fogarty, is scheduled to premiere November 25 on HBO Max.
 The event recognized several organizations and individuals advancing research and awareness.
 Dr. Jean Tang of Stanford University presented Innovation & Impact Awards to Children’s Hospital Colorado and the University of Colorado Anschutz.
 The institutions were recognized for research involving aggressive skin cancers associated with EB and the development of gene-corrected stem cell therapies.
 The gala also honored the late John Hudson Dilgen, an EB advocate who helped raise more than $720,000 for research before his death earlier this year.
 His mother, Faye Dilgen, presented the John Hudson Ambassadorship Award to Robbie Twible, another individual living with EB who advocates for the patient community.
 EBRP co-founder Jill Vedder subsequently presented Faye Dilgen with a second award recognizing her commitment to raising awareness.
 Additional leadership honors went to Glenn McGrath of Willis Towers Watson, Marc Seidner of PIMCO and philanthropist Dr. Jeff Heddles.
 Fundraising activities included a live auction featuring two guitars signed by Eddie Vedder and members of Pearl Jam. The auction and paddle raise generated more than $1.3 million.
 Founded in 2010, EB Research Partnership has raised more than $96 million and funded over 200 research projects across 22 countries.
 The organization reports that active EB clinical trials have increased from two to 50 since its founding.
 The U.S. Food and Drug Administration approved the first treatments for EB in 2023, and three treatments are now approved. According to EBRP, two were developed from scientific research the organization supported during its early stages.
 EBRP operates through a venture philanthropy model that allows the nonprofit to receive financial returns from successful research investments and reinvest those proceeds into additional projects.
 The organization is also expanding its approach to other rare diseases through Rare Ventures, an initiative launched with up to $25 million in support from the Richard King Mellon Foundation.
 The initiative brings together research and healthcare organizations including UPMC Children’s Hospital of Pittsburgh, Carnegie Mellon University, Stanford Medicine and ElevateBio.
 Venture Into Cures was presented by Willis Towers Watson and the McGrath Family, with additional support from several family foundations and sponsors.
 EB Research Partnership is a global nonprofit supporting research into epidermolysis bullosa and the development of potential treatments and cures for the disease.
